scope: First completed full-resolution occlusion-aware persistent-grasp adversarial audit
summary: The complete audit rejected the candidate because it incorrectly reused the visibility-resolved flower mask as persistent object state, while also independently retaining late hand-sharpness and structure-attack failures.
evidence: The audit completed 660 native 1280x720 frames in 297.0307 seconds at 2.2235 frames per second.
Ordinary late projected contact is 11/11, but source hold observability is only 28/147 and visual grasp recall is 19/147 when the person-core-eroded visibility mask is misused as object state.
Late hand edge energy violates its frozen lower limit in 22/180 frames and the structure-ghost attack delta p05 is 0.6086 below the fixed 0.75 gate.
Color, topology, and contact attacks are detected while the structure attack remains undetected.
lessons: A z-order visibility mask and an occlusion-persistent object-state mask are different variables and must never be silently substituted.
Improving persistent grasp cannot override independent hand-sharpness or adversarial-detector failures.
limitations: The completed audit does not establish a passing persistent-grasp result.
The candidate remains visual-only and cannot prove metric depth or force closure.
next_actions: Use the exact tracked flower occupancy only for the persistent interaction-state gate, retain the resolved-visible flower mask for rendering and ordinary projected-contact checks, and rerun without changing thresholds.
